findings.affected_surface: scripts/lib/review-fanout.js (job backstop timeout) and performFinalPanel seat launch path
findings.claim: The fan-out helper's per-job backstop timeout is set to --timeout + 60 s, so a seat whose dispatch-review.sh ignores or fails to enforce its own --timeout can consume up to 60 s beyond the panel consumer's remaining budget before SIGTERM, which is a bounded but real overshoot of the 'never handed more than its consumer's remaining budget' contract.
findings.evidence: Plan §1.2 states the helper's job timeout is 'a backstop at --timeout + 60 s (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 5 s)', while the seat's real budget bound is dispatch-review.sh's own rc=124 --timeout; R3's wording admits no overshoot of the consumer's remainder, and the engine suite's panel-timeout test asserts only the --timeout value, not the backstop margin.
findings.evidence_reference: Plan §1.2 (timeouts paragraph), §4 acceptance row panel-timeout; rubric R3
findings.repair: Clamp the helper's backstop for production panel seats to min(--timeout + 60 s, consumer-remaining-at-launch + 60 s) or record the backstop margin as informational overshoot in the design note and add an engine test that a stalled seat is killed within the backstop; no current change to the slice if the team accepts the documented 60 s margin as transport-failure territory.

findings.affected_surface: src/engine/autopilot-engine.js performFinalPanel ledger row emission; final_panel ledger schema (per-seat started_at/ended_at)
findings.claim: completion order is never observable in any artifact
findings.evidence: Plan §1.2 explicitly states: 'Timing fields (started_at/ended_at on ledger rows, elapsed) are informational, never digested, and are the one place concurrency is visible — by design (§5 reads them).' A parallel run's final_panel row therefore carries per-seat timestamps whose order reveals which seat finished first; §5 dogfood proof relies on this visibility ('overlap', 'slowest seat'). Strict reading of R1 says 'every artifact ... is identical to a sequential run in seat-index order; completion order is never observable', and per-row started_at/ended_at differ between the parallel and any sequential run, so the ledger rows are not byte-identical to a sequential run's.
findings.evidence_reference: docs/plans/2026-09-18-blind-review-panel-parallel.md §1.2 timing-field admission; §5 dogfood proof; existing ledger started_at/ended_at fields referenced in §0
findings.repair: No current code change; the design choice is explicit in §1.2. Pick one: (a) drop per-seat started_at/ended_at from the final_panel ledger row and record only the panel started_at/ended_at window so seat completion order is not exposed; (b) keep per-seat timestamps and amend the panel-execution paragraph plus R1 wording to make 'the one observable concurrency signal' explicit. The current 'informational, never digested' rationale does not satisfy the strict 'never observable' reading.
